targets.name: Transformed cultural allusion
targets.instruction: Score 10 when a recognizable song, film, text, or character is actively repurposed into the joke; score 0 when it is merely quoted or name-dropped.

targets.name: Teller as butt, with the admission doing comic work
targets.instruction: Score whether the narrator turns the joke on themselves AND the self-indictment is the payoff rather than a hedge. 10 = the speaker confesses something unflattering about their own habits, taste, or competence, and that confession is the funniest element in the item. 5 = self-deprecation is present but ornamental, an apology attached to a joke that works without it. 0 = no self-reference, or self-reference used purely to pre-excuse weak material.

targets.name: Surprise from withholding the expected punchline
targets.instruction: Score how much the text sets up an obvious punchline and then deliberately refuses to deliver it (or delivers something else), making the refusal itself the joke. 10 = the expected line is clearly implied but withheld; 0 = punchline delivered normally.

targets.name: Wordplay with homophone or near-homophone pivot
targets.instruction: Score how much the humor depends on a word sounding like another word with a different meaning. 10 = the entire joke is built around one homophone the reader must hear; 0 = no phonetic ambiguity is used.

targets.name: No self-explanation or apology attached to the pun
targets.instruction: Score whether the text lets the joke land unassisted. 10 = the punchline is delivered and nothing follows; the reader is trusted to notice. 5 = a brief flourish follows that adds something of its own. 0 = the text announces that a pun has occurred, names the device, or apologizes for the joke's quality.

targets.name: Insider knowledge gate with a self-verifying payoff
targets.instruction: Score the degree to which the joke requires a specific technical, scientific, mathematical or subcultural fact to decode, AND the payoff enacts that fact rather than merely mentioning it. 10 = decoding demands real domain knowledge and the punchline is a live demonstration of the very property invoked (a joke about an unreliable protocol that may not arrive; a number that is literally the square root of another). 5 = domain vocabulary appears but the gag reduces to a generic pun any reader could get. 0 = no specialist knowledge is needed or invoked at any point.

targets.name: References are load-bearing, not decorative name-drops
targets.instruction: For every shared reference the item invokes -- a named person, a product, a platform, a news event, a place, or an ordinary shared experience such as commuting or a doctor's waiting room -- ask whether the joke's mechanism actually exploits a specific property of it. Score 10 when each reference is load-bearing: the punch turns on something particular and true about that referent, and swapping it for a different referent of the same category would break the joke. An item containing no proper nouns, no slang and no topical material at all can score 10 if the ordinary shared situation it uses is exploited this precisely. Score 0 when references are decorative: the named person, brand or platform is interchangeable with any other, present only as recognition bait or to set a scene, and the punch would survive unchanged if you substituted a different name. Explicitly do NOT reward how many references there are, how current or recognisable they are, or how fashionable the vocabulary is; a single dense cluster of very recognisable names, none of which is exploited, scores 0. Do NOT judge whether the item is funny -- judge only whether its references do work.

targets.name: Setup supplies exactly what the punch needs to land
targets.instruction: Judge only whether the information needed for the joke's mechanism is present and correctly placed, in context. Ask: when the final line arrives, has the text already given the reader every premise, referent and detail that line depends on -- and has it withheld the thing the line reveals? Score 10 when the setup is complete and load-bearing: every pronoun has an antecedent, every referent the punch turns on has been introduced, nothing the punch needs arrives too late, and nothing that would spoil the punch arrives too early. A misspelt, lowercase, unpunctuated, run-on item can score 10 here if its logical scaffolding is intact and the punch has everything it needs. Score 0 when the mechanism cannot resolve: the punch relies on a fact, character or setting never supplied, an 'it' or 'he' points at nothing, the text stops before the mechanism completes, or the payload was already given away in the setup so nothing remains to land. Explicitly do NOT score spelling, capitalisation, punctuation, paragraph breaks, markup artifacts, or the polish of the prose; do NOT score whether the joke is funny -- an unfunny joke whose logic is fully supplied scores 10.

targets.name: Economy and timing of information release before the punch
targets.instruction: Judge the handling of information in this specific text, whatever shape it takes. Ask: is every element before the final beat doing work, and does the decisive element arrive last? Score 10 when the text is economical and correctly timed for its own content -- no sentence could be deleted without breaking the mechanism, no detail is repeated, no explanation follows the punch, no signposting tells the reader in advance what kind of turn is coming, and the word or phrase that flips the meaning sits at or near the end where it flips the most. A rambling-looking narrative can score 10 if each digression is a plant the ending uses; a one-line item can score 0 if half of it is redundant. Score 0 when the text wastes the reader: filler preamble, the same beat stated twice, the mechanism explained after it fires, or the revealing element buried in the middle so the ending merely restates it. Explicitly do NOT reward conformity to any template, do NOT reward shortness for its own sake, do NOT reward speaker labels, tidy layout or list formatting, and do NOT judge whether the item is funny; a flat joke with perfect information timing scores 10, and a hilarious one that explains itself afterwards scores low.

targets.name: Controlled anti-joke framing
targets.instruction: Score 10 when the text deliberately sets up a conventional joke expectation and makes banality, refusal, or withholding the actual payoff; score 0 when incompleteness appears accidental.

targets.name: Site-native self-reference that still executes a turn
targets.instruction: Composite. First, does the item draw on the culture of the posting forum itself - posting, reposting, karma, commenting, front page, the sub? If not, score 5 and stop. If it does, score whether the in-group material is used as the joke's mechanism rather than as its subject: 10 when the community reference sets up a genuine reversal, self-implication, or unexpected turn that would collapse if the community frame were removed; 0 when the item merely voices a familiar complaint about the community, or asserts community membership, with no turn at all. Insider vocabulary alone earns nothing.

targets.name: Textual coherence as a genuine joke vs. fragment/spam
targets.instruction: Score 10 if the text reads as a coherent, purposeful joke in fluent English. Score 0 if the text is incoherent, looks like ad copy/spam/keyword-stuffing, or is a fragment that doesn't cohere into any recognizable joke structure.

targets.name: Long scaffolding erected for one terminal pun
targets.instruction: Score the ratio of setup material to payoff. 10 = several sentences or paragraphs of narrative, list, or verse exist for no reason other than to make one final pun grammatical, and each setup clause is transparently reverse-engineered from the punchline. 5 = moderate setup, some of which does independent work. 0 = setup is one clause, or the setup is genuinely interesting on its own terms. Reward the diagnosis of reverse-engineered scaffolding, not length as such.

targets.name: Specialist-domain knowledge as the hinge
targets.instruction: Score whether the joke turns on a fact from a technical or specialist domain -- chemistry, mathematics, networking, physics, programming, psychoanalysis -- such that the reader must already hold that fact for the punchline to resolve. 10 = the hinge is a genuine domain fact, deployed accurately, and a reader without it gets nothing at all. 5 = a technical veneer over a joke that works anyway. 0 = no specialist content. Score the load the domain fact carries, not how hard the domain is.

targets.name: Platform self-awareness
targets.instruction: Score 10 when commentary on posting, reading, reposting, or forum behavior is itself part of the joke’s mechanism; score 0 when platform language is generic decoration.

targets.name: Phonetic double-use
targets.instruction: Score 10 when sound similarity creates two clear meanings that are quickly recoverable; score 0 when there is no phonetic mechanism or the resemblance is strained.

targets.name: Relatability of Frustration
targets.instruction: Score 10 if the joke taps into a widely shared everyday annoyance or social dynamic (addiction to scrolling, disappointment in content, petty logic) that readers feel personally. Score 0 if the premise is artificial or inaccessible.
